main_sampler.description: block-level parallel (semi-AR) diffusion sampling with causal ordering between blocks and KV-caching of previously generated blocks; within-block rule not stated

credited_component.text: Seed Diffusion Preview, a code-focused diffusion language model

design.other_detail: D01: mask-based absorbing corruption for the first 80% of diffusion training steps plus an added edit-based corruption (deletions, insertions, substitutions; edit count scheduled by a Levenshtein-style signal-to-noise ratio, alpha_t in [0, 0.1]) for the last 20%; not a plain mask-substitution mixture because insertions and deletions change the length. D15: Eq. 6, ELBO-weighted masked cross-entropy with the reconstruction term replaced by an edit-based denoising loss; then constrained-order trajectory fine-tuning (Eq. 9) and on-policy learning (Eq. 10).
design.inherited_from: standard mask-based corruption process [12, 15]; semi-AR block-level sampling [15, 26, 27]

evidence.quote: Seed Diffusion Preview is a discrete-state diffusion language model trained with two types of forward corruption process.
For the first 80% diffusion training steps, we use a standard mask-based corruption process [12, 15].

For the last 20% diffusion training steps, we add an extra edit-based corruption process as augmentation to improve calibration and eliminate unexpected behavior such as repetitions in the sampling process.
For the first 80% diffusion training steps, we use a standard mask-based corruption process [12, 15].
The forward process then samples a corrupted sequence based on a predefined edit operation set (e.g., deletions, insertions, and substitutions)
The corrupted sequence xt is sampled from the conditional distribution q(xt|x0) where each token is treated independently
We set the predicted probability over the mask token always as 0 [12] by adding −inf to the corresponding logits.
To balance computation and latency, we employ a block-level parallel diffusion sampling scheme that maintains a causal ordering between blocks.

Such a model learns a spurious correlation that unmasked tokens are always correct, leading to overconfidence and unable to perform self-correction during inference. To mitigate this, our edit-based augmentation forces the model to re-evaluate all tokens, including those unmasked

We use KV-caching for previously generated blocks to condition subsequent ones. Although this risks potentially introducing potential bias, we empirically observe no significant degradation in generation quality.
Our learning objective derives from ELBO in Eq. 6 by substituting the reconstruct loss with a denoised loss based on the edit-based forward process qedit
